plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Reduce AI/Software leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim income ETF (QQQI) to 20% to reduce concentration.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.
It aims for low, steady returns with minimal drawdown.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained.
conservative.read: This mode focuses on capital preservation, aiming for modest monthly gains around 1.5%. It significantly reduces leverage and concentrates on less volatile assets, accepting lower growth potential for a much lower risk of loss.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to low single digits.
Reduce AI/Software leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to small positions.
Maintain income ETF (QQQI) at 25% of the book.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
It aims for steady, risk-first growth around 2.5% per month.
A moderate cash buffer will be kept.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% monthly growth by reducing leverage and concentration. It blends broad market exposure with quality tech and limited leverage, aiming for consistent gains while managing downside risk.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to 6% each.
Increase AI/Software leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to 6% each.
Maintain income ETF (QQQI) at 25% of the book.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage.
It targets ~4% monthly returns but carries higher drawdown risk.
Leveraged ETF decay and strict stop discipline are critical.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode aims for high growth, targeting around 4% monthly returns by increasing leverage and concentration in strong setups. It accepts significantly higher potential drawdowns and requires strict stop discipline due to amplified risk and leveraged ETF decay.

plan: Sell all high-beta leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU).
Sell volatile growth stocks and sectors (SMH, CRWD, SNOW).
Eliminate AI/Software leveraged ETFs (METU, PLTU).
This plan prioritizes stable monthly income generation.
It aims for consistent distributions, not high growth.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained for stability.
income.read: This income-focused mode aims for steady monthly distributions around 1% by shifting to income-generating assets and broad indices. It minimizes volatility and growth potential to prioritize capital preservation and reliable cash flow, accepting that NAV can still decline in market downturns.
